{% raw %}
Setup is done entirely from Discord. You need to be a server administrator, or hold the Officer role once it is set (the setup wizard below is for server admins). Everything below replies privately, so nobody else sees your settings screens.

**Adding Alagos** to a server needs **Manage Server** there; the link is **alagos.gg/invite**. It asks only for what it uses: View Channels, Send Messages, Embed Links, Attach Files (event banners), Read Message History (so it can update its own posts), Create Public Threads (a thread on each event) and Manage Roles (role panels and roles for an event's sign-ups; Alagos's role must sit above the roles it gives). If a channel denies one of those -- officer-only channels often do -- give the Alagos role them in that channel, or the posts there fail. Alagos tells you which permission is missing when it can.

## The quick way: the setup wizard

When Alagos joins your server it posts two messages in your server's system channel: a welcome with **🧙 Start setup**, and a **📋 Setup checklist** of everything to set, marked ✅ done, ⬜ still to do, or ➖ fine as it is. The checklist keeps itself up to date as you set things, whether through the wizard or Guild Settings, so anyone helping you can see what is left.

**🧙 Start setup**, or `/setup` at any time, walks you through it privately, one step a screen, in the same order as the Guild Settings tabs:

1. **The basics**: your timezone, what Alagos calls your group, and who receives "Archon only" feedback.
2. **Roles**: your Officer role, and a Senior role if you have one, picked straight from a menu.
3. **Channels**: where events, reminders, claims, logs and feedback go. Each channel is checked as you pick it.
4. **Features and limits**: the defaults, which suit most servers. Press Next to keep them.
5. **Panels**: the member panel and the officer panel.
6. **Your game**: switch on DC Dark Legion, or carry on with no game.
7. **The game's own settings**: for DC Dark Legion, its channels, Guardian cities and train and Guardian eligibility.
8. **All done**: what is left, and your first event.

**Each step saves as soon as you finish it**, so you can skip anything, close the wizard and come back with `/setup`: it opens at the first step still to do. The wizard is for **server admins**: a Discord administrator, or a role holding Alagos's **Admin** bundle. Officers can still change everything on `/guild-settings show`.

If Alagos could not post in your system channel, the welcome goes to the server owner by DM instead, without the checklist: run `/setup` in the server, and press **📋 Post the setup checklist here** on its last step to put the checklist in any channel you like.

The rest of this guide covers each setting in more detail, tab by tab.

## 1. See what is missing

Run `/guild-settings show`. The **Overview** tab is a checklist of the four things Alagos needs before it is useful:

- your **timezone**, confirmed
- an **Officer role** (or an Admin role)
- an **Officer Log** channel
- an **Event Post** channel

It also shows which game modules are on. Come back to it at any point; it says **Setup complete** once those four are done. A change takes effect at once.

Every setting is changed on the panel itself: each tab has buttons that open a short form, already filled in with what is set now.

## 2. Set your timezone

Every time you type into the bot or read from it uses your server's timezone, and **a new server starts on New York's**. On the **Overview** tab press **🕒 Timezone**, pick your region, then your timezone. Each one shows how far it is from UTC today and a place you know, for example **UTC−05:00 · New York (Eastern)**. Picking the one already chosen confirms it. Not listed? Press **Other…** and type its name, for example `America/Chicago` or `Europe/London`. If the name is not quite right, the bot suggests the ones you probably meant.

Recurring events repeat on a fixed 24-hour clock, so after a daylight-saving change an event set for 18:00 may show an hour earlier or later. Edit its time if that matters to you.

## 3. Choose your officer role

On the **Roles** tab press **🛡️ Open permissions**, then pick the Discord role your officers have under **Officer**. You can pick more than one role. Until an Officer role is set, only server administrators can manage the bot. Server administrators can always do everything.

There is also a **Senior** tier for trusted members who are not officers. It is optional; officers automatically have everything a senior can do.

**🤖 Automatic roles**, also on the **Roles** tab, are roles Alagos gives and takes by itself from what it knows about each member, so the right channels open without anyone pressing anything:

- **On the roster**: a member whose character claim is approved. A good way to open your members' channels.
- **Plays a game**: a member with a character in that game.
- **On leave** (Premium): while they are marked on leave. They keep the roster role.
- **A game detail** (Premium): for example a role for each DC Dark Legion rank. One rule is one value, so add a rule per rank.

Press **➕ Add a rule**, choose who gets it and which role. Alagos tells you how many people it will go to before you confirm, then gives it to everyone it fits and keeps it up to date as claims, characters, leave and ranks change. Only members linked to their character get automatic roles. A player marked inactive loses them all. Removing a rule takes its role off again. A role a member already had before Alagos is never taken away, and a role two rules give stays while either still applies.

Roles with a moderation or admin permission, and roles you have given an Alagos permission (such as your Officer role), are refused, so editing someone's rank can never promote them. Alagos needs **Manage Roles**, with its own role above these. If someone takes an automatic role off by hand in Discord, Alagos does not notice and leaves it off; give it back by hand.

## 4. Pick your channels

On the **Channels** tab, the two buttons open forms with a channel picker for each kind of channel. The ones that matter most:

- **Officer Log**: where the bot reports problems and sends officer notices. Set this first.
- **Event Post**: where new events are posted.
- **Event Reminder**: where reminders go. Without it, reminders go to the event's own channel.
- **Claim Requests**: where members' character claims wait for an officer. Without it, they go to the Officer Log.
- **Anonymous Feedback**: where members' anonymous feedback arrives. Without it, it goes to the Officer Log.
- **Feedback Answers**: where public replies to feedback are posted. Pick a channel your members can read; this one has no fallback.
- **Audit Log**: a running record of what the bot did and who asked it to. Optional.

Make sure the bot can see and post in each channel you pick; if it cannot, the panel says so as soon as you save. Leaving a picker empty clears that channel.

## 5. Decide who can do what (optional)

Run `/guild-settings permissions`. Each **bundle** has a role picker under it: pick the roles that hold it.

- **Admin**: everything, including settings. Only server administrators can change who is Admin.
- **Officer**: runs the league: events, attendance, the roster, rotations, teams, reports and settings.
- **Senior**: trusted members who can see how the rotations are treating people.

Server administrators always have everything. Picking `@everyone`, or a role another bot manages, is refused.

**Rename titles** lets you call the bundles what your community calls them, for example "R4" for Officer. The new names show in the panel and when someone is told they do not have permission.

**Advanced: single actions** gives one job to another role as well, for example letting a Recruiter role **Manage the roster**. This is part of a premium plan; removing a role you added is always possible. Your Officer roles keep every job whatever you pick.

**More than one game or group?** Once your server has two, **By game or group** appears. There you can make someone **Game Manager** for one game, or **Group Leader** for one group, and give Officer or Senior for just that game or group (the Community plan). A Game Manager or Group Leader can open `/guild-settings permissions` themselves: they see only their own game or group, and can give the places below theirs there. A Game Manager can also change their game's settings: `/guild-settings show` opens on their game's tab.

## 6. Put up the panels

On the **Panels** tab, set up two panels, each a message with buttons the bot keeps up to date:

- **Member panel**, in a channel your members can see: **My profile**, **Claim my character**, **Send feedback** and **Help**.
- **Officer panel**, in a channel only officers can see: **New event**, **Events**, **Record attendance**, **Roster**, **Claim requests**, **Feedback**, [**Reports**](/guides/reports/) and **Settings**, plus a game's own buttons (DC Dark Legion adds **Run train**, **Run Guardian** and **Teams**). It also shows how many claim requests and feedback items are waiting.

Pick the channel and tick the buttons you want. Each button opens privately, for the person who pressed it, and checks their permission as the matching command does. If a panel is deleted, the bot posts it again.

**🎭 Role panels**, on the same tab, are panels of buttons members press to take a role, for example the game they play or the region they are in:

1. **➕ New panel**: a title, a line under it, the channel, and whether members may take **any number** of its roles or **only one** (taking one drops the others).
2. **➕ Add a role**: pick it, and give it a button label and an emoji if you like. Up to 20 roles a panel.
3. **📤 Post it.** Later changes redraw the posted panel by themselves.

**A panel for the welcome flow only** needs no channel: leave **Post in** empty, and it is never posted -- its buttons appear only as a step of the 👋 welcome flow below. Give it a channel later under **Edit** to post it as well; empty the channel again and its post comes down.

Pressing a button gives the role; pressing it again takes it away. Roles that carry a moderation or admin permission (kick, ban, manage roles, mention everyone and so on) are never offered, so a button can never hand out power. Alagos needs **Manage Roles**, and its own role must sit above the roles it gives: in Server Settings → Roles, drag the Alagos role up. The **Free** plan allows 3 role panels, a paid plan 25.

**🧩 Custom panels**, on the same tab, are your own button panels, for a raid team, recruitment or your stewards:

1. **➕ New panel**: a name (only officers see it), the title on the panel and a short text.
2. **➕ Add buttons**: any button from the member and officer panels, and **shortcuts** to things you have made: a championship's standings (and, for a league of teams, Report a result, Confirm a result and Check in), an application form's Apply, an event template's New event, or a role panel's roles. **🔗 Add a link** for your website or rules. Up to 20 buttons, 5 of them links.
3. Pick a button to move it up or down, rename it, or remove it.
4. **🔒 Who may press it**: everyone, or only the roles you choose. Discord shows a panel to everyone who can see its channel, so for a few people, also put it in a channel only they can see. Each button's own permission still applies.
5. **📌 Post it.** Changes redraw it by themselves, and it comes back if deleted.

The **Free** plan allows 2 custom panels, Premium 15.

**👋 Welcome flow**, on the same tab, is one **🧙 Start here** message that walks newcomers through your server privately, step by step, with Alagos as a (light-hearted) wizard:

1. **The rules**: your rules and **✅ I agree**, which gives an "agreed" role. In Discord, open your channels to that role and keep the Start here channel open to everyone: people agree before they see the rest.
2. **Pick your roles**: one of your role panels as a step, for the games they play, their region or platform.
3. **Your character** (when a game is on): **Claim my character**, or **Add my character** if your game lets members add their own. A good moment to get everyone on the roster.
4. **The finish**: they're all set.

Press **Channel and intro** to choose the channel, add the steps from the **➕ Add a step** menu, then **📤 Post it**. Pressing **Start here** again lets people change their roles or claim later. That is the free setup. A paid plan adds **questions** whose answers give a role, show a message or open a form (a question must be answered before going on); up to five role-pick steps; your own wording on every step, the intro and the finish (or Alagos speaking plainly); and links on the finish.

A question is answered in one of three ways: **pick one of the answers**; **pick an answer, or type one under ✏️ Other…**; or **type an answer** (up to 500 characters), for things like "Which leagues have you been in?". Don't ask for anything personal, such as an email address or a real name. Each member's latest answer is kept: **📋 Answers**, on the welcome flow and on each question, shows how many picked each answer and who answered what, newest first, one answer at a time if you like, with **📄 Export CSV**. Answering again replaces a member's answer, and someone coming back does not have to answer again. Removing a question deletes its answers (Alagos says how many first). Whoever can set up the welcome flow can read the answers.

## 7. Make your first event

Run `/event-create` with a title, a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and a time (`HH:MM`, 24-hour, your server's time). The event editor opens. Its tabs:

- **Core Info**: title, description, event type, banner.
- **Schedule**: channel, time, duration, and whether it repeats (weekly, every two weeks, every other day).
- **Signups**: whether members can sign up, the answer buttons and their labels, a limit on numbers, when signups close, and whether attendance is recorded.
- **Notifications**: a reminder before it starts, a role to ping, and how early each week's event is posted. A role is only pinged if it allows **@mention by anyone** (Server Settings → Roles → the role); the editor warns you when it does not.

**💾 Save** keeps your changes; **📢 Post to channel** puts the event up for members. `/event-list` reopens the editor later. The Officers guides cover events in detail.

## 8. Playing DC Dark Legion?

Run `/guild-settings modules` and press **Switch on** beside DC Dark Legion. Its commands appear within a few seconds. The [**DC Dark Legion setup**](/guides/dcdl-setup/) guide covers its extra channels, Guardian cities and schedules. Switching a module off hides it and keeps all its data.

## 9. Your plan and the support server

New servers start on the **Free** plan: up to 5 upcoming one-off events and 3 repeating events at a time. Weekly occurrences of a repeating event do not count. `/tier view` shows your plan and what you are using.

**A free trial of Premium.** If the Alagos team gave you a code, press **🎟️ Redeem a code** on `/tier view` (on the Free plan, for whoever manages settings). Premium is on until the date shown there, and your officers' log channel is told three days before it ends. When it ends, the server goes back to Free and nothing is deleted. Each server can have one free trial.

`/tier view` also has **🎫 Get support server token**. Join the Alagos support server, press **Verify your server** on its pinned message and paste the token: you get the role for your plan, and can report bugs, request features and ask for help there. A token works once and lasts 24 hours.

## Extras

- **✏️ What we're called** on the **Overview** tab renames what Alagos calls your group ("League" for DC Dark Legion, "Guild" with no game) -- for example **Alliance** / **Alliances**. Leave it blank to go back to the default.
- **🏷️ Event types** on the **Features & limits** tab adds your own event types beside the built-in ones (5 on the Free plan, 25 on paid plans). A type an event has used can be retired but not deleted.
- **✏️ Edit features & limits** on the **Features & limits** tab turns automatic discussion threads on event posts on or off (on by default), and holds the smaller settings: how long attendance can be edited, how often unclaimed players are reminded, how long handled feedback is kept, and which day the weekly feedback summary is sent. Leave a number blank to go back to its default.
- **📚 Game lists** on a game's tab (for games that have lists, such as classes or raids) shows the choices Alagos offers for that game. If something is missing, such as a class added in a new patch, press **➕ Add**: it is for your server only, at once. Up to 10 additions per game on the Free plan. Renaming or hiding a built-in entry needs a paid plan. An entry a character already has is retired rather than deleted.
- **🔔 Notifications** on the **Features & limits** tab chooses which personal messages Alagos may send members of this server (event reminders, event changes, off the bench, claim decisions, and your game's own). All are on by default; members also choose their own in `/my-profile`. Unticking one stops it for everyone.
- **📬 Weekly summary** on the **Features & limits** tab posts last week's attendance for officers on the day you choose, at 18:00 your time: events held, attendances against the week before, by type, the most active members, and how many have gone quiet. It goes to the channel you pick, or the Officer Log. Paid plans.
- **🔒 Archon** on the **Overview** tab chooses who receives anonymous feedback marked **Archon only**. Their DMs must be open to server members.
